 4. Legal basis and its application to this request

 Evidence and time to comply. Regulation 38 of the 2013 Claims and Payments Regulations governs
 information in connection with an award and refers, for regulation 38(2) requests, to regulation
 45(4)(a) of the 2013 Decisions and Appeals Regulations. Where regulation 45 applies, notification and
 the applicable period matter; the latter includes provision for a longer period necessary to comply.
 Please identify the provision and notice actually relied on and decide my request for time against my
 circumstances. I do not assert that every review attracts a new fixed period or that this update resets
 an existing deadline. [L1-L2.]

 Original documents and support. DWP's review guidance requires documents without changes or
 edits and directs claimants to the review agent for help with format or provision. I request that
 assistance and a current approved route. My supplementary reading copy does not replace the
 unchanged originals. [L3.]

 SAR. UK GDPR Articles 12 and 15 and the ICO's current subject-access guidance require a response
 without undue delay, ordinarily within one month, subject to lawful timing provisions. A request need
 not name the right team or use a prescribed form. If DWP received my 17 July request then, the
 ordinary period would have passed before 10 October; please identify any different receipt date,
 necessary identity/clarification step, extension and notice rather than treating a later referral as a new
 request. [L4.]

 Data-protection complaint. DPA 2018 section 164A, inserted by DUAA 2025 section 103 and in force
 from 19 June 2026, requires acknowledgment within 30 days of receipt and appropriate response
 steps, progress information and the outcome without undue delay. The 30 days are for
 acknowledgment, not a universal deadline to complete the investigation. Please explain compliance for
 the separate 31 August complaint, including the receipt date and copies of any response. [L5-L6.]

 Privacy and accuracy. UK GDPR Article 5 requires, among other things, relevant and limited
 processing, accuracy, appropriate retention and security, and accountability. Please address my
 specific handling questions and any inaccurate factual record. These principles do not alone prove that
 the UC upload process was insecure or give me a general right to redact required evidence. [L7.]

 Fair participation and challenge. Osborn v Parole Board [2013] UKSC 61, paragraphs 67-71,
 explains the value of relevant information, participation and respect in administrative fairness. I rely on
 that general principle, not a universal entitlement to an oral hearing in this review. Please explain the
 actual decision and route for challenging it. GOV.UK gives the usual mandatory-reconsideration period
 as one month from the decision date, subject to the applicable rules and exceptions; a complaint or
 SAR does not itself extend that period. [L8-L9.]

 For the service complaint, DWP's published procedure describes escalation to the complaints team and
 a usual 15-working-day aim, currently qualified by high volumes. Please give the actual owner and
 expected response date for my complaint. This service route is separate from a benefit-decision
 challenge and the statutory data-protection complaint. [L10.]
